story.conflict: The daughter understands that her father is lonely but refuses to help him turn his wife's care needs into permission to deceive her.
story.hook: Dad brought his girlfriend to visit his wife. He asked me to introduce her to Mom as a nurse.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE DESERVED THE TRUTH
story.premise: A father brings his girlfriend to visit his wife in a care home and asks their daughter to introduce the girlfriend as a nurse.
story.punchline: He'd said Mom wouldn't notice. She'd noticed who left.
story.script: I asked why he couldn't introduce her himself. He said Mom trusted me and wouldn't ask questions if I said it. Mom had been having trouble with her memory. I told him that didn't make his girlfriend a nurse. He said I knew how lonely he'd been since Mom moved there. I said we could talk about that without making up somebody's job. His girlfriend asked what we were whispering about. When I told her, she said he'd described this as a friendly visit. Dad said Mom wouldn't notice, so nobody needed to make it complicated. Then he asked me to take a picture of all of us so my brother could see how well everyone was getting along. I put my phone away. He said if every visit turned into a trial, perhaps I should come on my own. I asked whether he was really making seeing Mom depend on me helping with this. His girlfriend put her bag back on her shoulder and said she wasn't going to pretend to work there. Dad followed her toward the lift, telling me I'd made her feel unwelcome. Mom asked whether he was staying for tea. I said he'd gone downstairs. She pushed the extra cup toward me and asked me to stay instead. I sat down. He'd said Mom wouldn't notice. She'd noticed who left.
story.twist: The girlfriend was not told about the false introduction, and the father's insistence that his wife notices nothing is contradicted by the person she sees leaving.

youtube.description: A daughter refuses to disguise her father's new relationship as part of her mother's care.
youtube.title: The Nurse Dad Wanted Me to Introduce

story.conflict: Her ex expects her to endorse a history of care that erases his abandonment and gives him paid access to her home again.
story.hook: I found my ex claiming he'd been my full-time carer. He'd left me after saying he couldn't live like that.
story.premise: A woman finds her ex claiming years of nonexistent caring experience while applying to become her paid caregiver.
story.punchline: He'd put our marriage down as experience. I remembered it as being left alone.
story.script: The assessor asked me to confirm the experience on his application. The dates covered years we'd lived apart. I asked him what he'd actually done for me during them. He said this wasn't the time to go through our marriage. After my accident, he'd said he couldn't live like that and left. I asked why he'd applied for this job when he'd refused to do those same things before. He said it was different when there was a wage and a proper schedule. Then he asked me to tell the assessor we'd always worked well together. I said we hadn't. He laughed and said I was still angry about the divorce. I told him I could be divorced and still need someone reliable to help me. The assessor asked whether I wanted to continue the meeting with him there. Before I answered, he said finding another worker could take weeks, and I shouldn't make life harder for myself to prove a point. I said I wanted the assessment to continue, but not his application. He asked whether I was really going to cost him a job over the past. I told him he was the one asking me to sign that past off as experience. After he left, I explained which tasks I wanted help with and which I wanted to do myself. He'd put our marriage down as experience. I remembered it as being left alone.
story.twist: When she refuses to confirm his experience, he recasts her right to choose support as an attempt to punish him and threatens her with a longer wait for help.

youtube.description: An ex-husband's job application asks the person he abandoned to certify that he stayed.
youtube.title: The Caring Years on His Application

story.conflict: Workers who need their final wages are pressured to pay their former boss for a commission-only opportunity and sell it to their equally vulnerable coworkers.
story.hook: Our boss turned the layoff meeting into a sales pitch. He'd put starter kits under our chairs and wanted us to buy our way back to work.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF WAGES COME BEFORE SALES
story.premise: A boss turns a layoff meeting into a pitch for departing employees to buy sales kits and recruit one another.
story.punchline: He still wouldn't tell us when we'd be paid for last week.
story.script: He told us to look under our seats before anyone asked about final wages. There were boxes of cleaning products with our names on them. He said the office was closing, but we could become independent sellers instead. I asked whether that meant a salary. He said we'd earn what we deserved to earn. Then he brought out the card machine. The kit cost more than my grocery money for the month. My coworker asked whether we could try selling first and pay afterward. He said people needed to invest in themselves. When I asked again about last week's pay, he told me negative attitudes would follow people into their next jobs. Then he reminded us he was still the person employers would call for references. My coworker started taking out her credit card. He told me I could earn my kit price back by signing her up under me. She'd worked beside me for four years. Now he wanted me to make money from getting her to pay him. I told her I wasn't recommending something I wouldn't buy myself. She asked him whether anyone had actually earned back the fee. He began talking about positive thinking again. We left our boxes under the chairs and walked out together. He called us his new partners. He still wouldn't tell us when we'd be paid for last week.
story.twist: The promised independence still requires buying the boss's stock, supplying his recruits, and accepting his influence over their references.

youtube.description: A final staff meeting offers independence with a price tag and the same boss holding the references.
youtube.title: The Starter Kits Under Our Layoff Chairs

story.conflict: He treats his wife's working hours as permission for his dates while expecting her own free time and loyalty to remain exclusively his.
story.hook: My husband said my coffee date was cheating. His dinner dates were allowed because I was working nights.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF RULES APPLY BOTH WAYS
story.premise: A husband who declares their marriage open during his wife's night shifts calls her planned coffee date cheating.
story.punchline: My shift still started at seven. I wasn't coming home after it.
story.script: I asked him to explain the difference. He said his dates filled time when I wasn't available, while mine would take time away from us. The coffee was on my day off. I reminded him he'd said we were free to see other people. He said I'd taken that too literally. When he'd first brought it up, I'd asked whether the same rules applied to both of us. He'd told me grown adults shouldn't need a rule book. Now he wanted the name of the man I'd agreed to meet. I said I wasn't giving him somebody's number so he could interfere. He said if there was nothing to hide, I could call and cancel in front of him. Then he asked whether I was planning to embarrass him by telling people our marriage was open. I asked why I should have to hide something he kept calling healthy. He said his dates didn't mean anything, but mine sounded like I wanted a different life. I told him I was starting to. I contacted the man myself and said I wasn't ready to date, and I was sorry I'd brought him into an argument. My husband said he was glad I'd come to my senses. Then he saw the overnight bag beside my work shoes. My shift still started at seven. I wasn't coming home after it.
story.twist: Her decision is not to win equal permission from him but to stop treating another person as a test of rules her husband keeps changing.

youtube.description: A coffee invitation exposes an open marriage with permission for only one partner.
youtube.title: The Rule That Only Applied on Night Shifts

story.conflict: The ex tries to turn a space for her recovery into an audience for his reconciliation pitch, using his payment for the room as a claim on her attention.
story.hook: My ex brought flowers into my divorce support group. He asked the women there to convince me to take him back.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SUPPORT ISN'T A VOTE
story.premise: A woman's ex brings flowers to her divorce support group and asks its members to persuade her to reconcile.
story.punchline: For once, I didn't have to stand beside him in it.
story.script: He stood between me and the empty chair I'd been about to take. I asked him to leave. He said he'd only need five minutes if everyone would listen with an open mind. One woman said perhaps hearing him out would help me move on. He handed her the flowers and said that was exactly what he meant. I told her moving on didn't have to mean going back. Then he announced he'd paid that month's room hire through a friend. The volunteer who organized the meetings said she hadn't known the money came from him. He said surely that meant he deserved a chance to speak. I told him paying for a room didn't buy my answer. He started passing around photographs from our wedding and asking whether we looked like people who should give up. I said I wasn't going to explain our marriage to a roomful of people so they could vote on it. The woman holding the flowers put them on a table. She said she'd come because her own family kept telling her to give somebody another chance. She hadn't meant to do the same thing to me. My ex asked whether she was really siding with a stranger over a husband. She moved her chair beside mine. I finally sat down. He was still holding our wedding photograph. For once, I didn't have to stand beside him in it.
story.twist: A member who initially urges her to hear him out recognizes that the group's job is not to help him obtain the answer he wants.

youtube.description: An ex-husband buys room hire, then discovers the group's support is not his to direct.
youtube.title: The Flowers at My Divorce Support Group
